pending_commit.commit_message: coral: chromeos-config dep on chromeos-bsp-coral. In some cases, while building packages for coral, we would fail with a stacktrace shown below because /usr/share/chromeos-config/config.dtb did not exist. To ensure it gets populated before running the installation of chromeos-bsp-coral, add a dependency on chromeos-config. In addition, the unibuild USE flag must be set in public, since otherwise a lot of the dependencies in the system won't be correct, e.g. the media-sound/adhd package won't depend on chromeos-config as it should. firmware: tpm2_lite: propagate actual errors Propagate the actual error - a non-successful response code from the tpm or communication/serializing failure - to the caller of the Tlcl functions in TPM 2.0 case. Currently, the callers only have special processing for the error codes from TCG TPM 1.2 range, which are never returned in case of communication or serialization failures or from the actual TPM 2.0. (The only case of mapping TPM 2.0 error codes to TPM_E_BADINDEX is preserved in this CL.) Thus, changing the actual values returned from the functions won't change any current behavior in the calling layers. This CL is a preparatory work for adding special processing for communication errors in mount-encrypted. BUG=chromium:702724 BRANCH=none TEST=build; test that tpmc getvf, tpmc read still work. BACKPORT: mm/madvise.c: fix madvise() infinite loop under special circumstances commit 6ea8d958a2c95a1d514015d4e29ba21a8c0a1a91 upstream. MADVISE_WILLNEED has always been a noop for DAX (formerly XIP) mappings. Unfortunately madvise_willneed() doesn't communicate this information properly to the generic madvise syscall implementation. The calling convention is quite subtle there. madvise_vma() is supposed to either return an error or update &prev otherwise the main loop will never advance to the next vma and it will keep looping for ever without a way to get out of the kernel. It seems this has been broken since introduction. Nobody has noticed because nobody seems to be using MADVISE_WILLNEED on these DAX mappings. firwmare_Cr50OpenWhileAPOff: modify how devices are held in reset Boards like bob cannot tell that the AP is off when the EC is held in reset. During init determine the level of deep sleep support. If Cr50 cannot tell the AP is off when the EC is in reset, just rely on turning the AP off. Skip trying to fully open cr50, because the power button presses required to open cr50 would turn on the AP. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=run on bob and reef. Make sure it fails with 2.1 and passes with 3.3 Change-Id: If1e24b1ee3dc5618f623114c82e5d6057f254856 Signed-off-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/978669 Commit-Ready: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>

firmware_Cr50CCDServoCap: ignore the I2C state flag Due to hardware limitations, the I2C flag may not be useful. Use SPI, and AP/EC TX as a good enough indicator for what cr50 is trying to do with ccdstate. Ignore I2C. BUG=b:76108297 BRANCH=none TEST=run with 2.1 and 3.3.
